layers.note: A fern of wet forest hollows, stream banks, seeps and swamp margins.

heat_load.note: Favours cool, shaded aspects and ravines; scarce on hot south-west slopes.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

sun_tolerance.note: Grows in sun only where the ground stays wet; its fronds scorch in dry sun.

coldest_c.note: Very cold winters borne: coldest-month means from about −25 °C (gone by −35 °C), as across the boreal forest.

hard_freeze_c.note: Among the hardiest: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Short, cool summers suffice: warmest-month means from about 11.5 °C, the tree line's warmth, up to about 22.5 °C; gone below 9 °C and above 26 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 700.

degree_days_5.note: A short growing season suffices: about 450 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 200.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.55, gone by 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No limit in its range: summer-dry coasts to continental summer rain.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Lady fern is circumboreal in moist forest and by streams (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
